tweets.author: firsthandbitcoin.com
tweets.text:
Most businesses move to where their customers are.
Bitcoin mining moves to where the power has none.

That's where the cheapest bitcoin gets made.

firsthandbitcoin.com/data/cost-t...

tweets.author: firsthandbitcoin.com
tweets.text:
Put a generator at the well and a container of mining machines beside it.

The gas makes electricity. The electricity makes bitcoin.

No pipeline, no power line, no customer for miles. The site needs one thing from the outside world: an internet connection.

tweets.author: firsthandbitcoin.com
tweets.text:
The usual picture of bitcoin mining: giant buildings on the same grid as your house, competing with you for every kilowatt.

The cheapest bitcoin is often made somewhere with no grid at all.

tweets.author: firsthandbitcoin.com
tweets.text:
For decades, oil wells have burned off about 150 billion cubic metres of gas a year, on purpose, for nothing.

In 2011 that was about a quarter of all the gas the US used in a year.

Bitcoin mining is one of the few things that can turn it into money.
